title: Automation and New Tasks: How Technology Displaces and Reinstates Labor
what_it_gives_you: The frame your argument has to live in: technology both displaces and reinstates labor. Any displacement claim that ignores reinstatement is incomplete.

title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
what_it_gives_you: The occupation-level exposure index most later work cites. Start here for the measurement side and for its limits: capability overlap is not adoption.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Jobs: Evidence from Online Vacancies
what_it_gives_you: Closest thing to causal evidence in the stack: establishment-level vacancy postings rather than occupation scores.

title: The simple macroeconomics of AI
what_it_gives_you: The strongest modest-effects counterargument. Read it to know what you are arguing against before you argue.

title: Gen-AI
what_it_gives_you: Cross-country exposure estimates, and the international comparison your Indonesia vantage point should engage.

title: Measuring the Occupational Impact of AI: Tasks Cognitive Abilities and AI Benchmarks
what_it_gives_you: Task-to-AI-benchmark mapping. Use it if you build your own exposure score instead of borrowing one.

title: Generative AI and Firm Values
what_it_gives_you: Market-implied exposure: what equity valuations say about exposure. Useful as a contrast because prices are forward-looking in a way employment data is not.

title: Economics of ChatGPT: a labor market view on the occupational impact of artificial intelligence
venue: Journal of Electronic Business & Digital Economics
what_it_gives_you: Occupational exposure applied specifically to ChatGPT. Narrower and less cited, but current and readable.
